text:
ryan: Flagging postmortem follow-up from the throughput/latency incident. Pattern: large-batch bursts plus many concurrent long-context requests caused backpressure and reduced overall throughput. Need SLO/SLA changes that cover both latency and throughput, owners for dashboarding, and admission-control mitigations.

mei: Agree. This one is more throughput-y than the previous tail issues. Small requests were starved because GPUs were saturated by a handful of massive requests.

chaim: Propose a combined SLO set: keep p95 strict for interactive traffic, and add a throughput SLO (qps_per_gpu) for the dedicated pool so we can reason about capacity. Also add a short-term admission-control rule for token-heavy requests.

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-421 | Sev2 | start=2180000000 | end=2180000600 | primary=serving-runtime | link=https://redwood.internal/incidents/2026-421

ryan: Draft SLOs (open for feedback):
```
- name: inference_latency_interactive
  objective:
    window: 30d
    targets:
      p95: <= 210ms
      p99: <= 800ms  # temporary guard while admission-control is enabled
- name: serving_throughput_dedicated
  objective:
    window: 7d
    targets:
      qps_per_gpu: >= 120  # measured at 95th percentile over 1h windows
```
Notes: qps_per_gpu target helps detect large requests that drop effective throughput. We'll re-evaluate after admission-control and batching scheduler changes.

mei: For admission-control I propose token-aware knobs:
- global burst quota pool (X tokens/sec) for heavy requests
- token-cost accounting per request (approx tokens * compute multiplier)
- when token budget exhausted -> soft-deny with Retry-After header and `X-Redwood-Fallback` note
This is less disruptive than blanket fallback to smaller models.

chaim: Also add a circuit-breaker: if GPU queueing latency > 300ms for >2m, automatically reduce allowed token-budget by 30% and enable compact-model routing for new long requests. Auto-revert after 10m of stable telemetry.

ops: Dashboard ownership: I'll take the per-GPU throughput panels and the admission-control telemetry. Plan: add metrics: qps_per_gpu, avg_batch_size, token_budget_remaining, admission_denied_rate, backpressure_events. ETA: 5 working days (2026-04-15).

ryan: Alerts suggested:
- sustained qps_per_gpu < 100 for 10m -> page (possible overload)
- admission_denied_rate > 2% for 5m -> warn channel
- gpu_queue_latency > 300ms for 3m -> page + auto-circuit triggered

mei: Runbook updates: add steps to drain heavy-request pools, manually set token budget, and enable fallback routing. I'll own runbook edits (due 2026-04-12).

sre-bot: Reminder created: "Throughput & Admission-control sync" 2026-04-13 16:00 UTC. Owner: @ops

chaim: Action items recap:
- ryan: open SLO PR with qps_per_gpu metric + measurement doc (due 2026-04-10)
- ops: dashboard + alert PR (first pass due 2026-04-15)
- mei: implement token-aware admission-control prototype in staging and run perf sim (due 2026-04-14)
- chaim: add CI perf test that simulates mixed load (90% small interactive, 10% massive-batch) and gate SLO PR on it (due 2026-04-11)
- ops: include error-budget burn chart and explicit owner field for each alert (dashboard requirement)

ryan: Rollback / gating rules:
- If admission-control increases client error rate (5xx or 429) attributable to policy by >1% for 10m -> rollback to previous config
- If throughput SLO drops under 80 qps_per_gpu for >15m during canary -> abort rollout
- Require quality sampling for any fallback routing (sampled outputs saved to private bucket, automated quality check)

mei: Quality check plan: sample 5% of fallback responses, run lightweight similarity metric vs baseline and surface any drift >4% to the channel. If drift detected, disable fallback in canary.

ops: I'll add dashboard panels for the quality sampling pass rate and a link to the sample store. Also will tag alerts with pager ownership (oncall rotation).

chaim: One more ask: add a short-term throughput SLA note for Dedicated customers explaining the temporary protective measures (admission-control) so sales/support can pre-communicate. I'll draft a customer note if someone from support approves.

ops: I'll draft the note and loop in support for signoff. ETA: 2026-04-13.

ryan: PR links will be posted here once opened. Let's keep a 2-week check cadence for throughput telemetry until metrics are stable for 30 days.

ops: Ack. Opening ticket in postmortem tracker and assigning owners. If deadlines slip, flag here. :thumbsup:
